name: Ines Varo
summary: Determined apprentice cartographer to Maestro Kell. She discovers his hidden charts documenting an impossible bay that will open in the future, and commits herself to completing his work. Patient and meticulous, she refuses to surrender knowledge to those who would exploit it for profit, becoming a master cartographer in her own right.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Young adult (early 20s implied)

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Apprentice cartographer, later official city cartographer

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To understand and protect Maestro Kell's knowledge; to listen to the water as he did

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: That the water's secrets will be corrupted by greed and institutional control

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Calm, precise, contemplative; speaks only after careful thought

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The Lighthouse Chart

name: Maestro Kell
summary: Renowned cartographer and Ines's master. He discovers the bay hidden in the future through decades of patient observation and measurement. He documents this impossible knowledge in a copper-bound folder, then drowns mysteriously during a spring survey. His charts and philosophy guide Ines long after his death.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Elderly (deceased before narrative begins)

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Master cartographer, listener to the water

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To understand the water's true nature and patterns

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: That his knowledge will be misused for profit and power

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Thoughtful, precise notation; communicates through careful letters and marginal notes

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The Lighthouse Chart (legacy)

name: Thren
summary: Maestro Kell's second apprentice, preferring accounts and numbers to the uncertainty of water-watching. He works in the harbour office and helps Ines protect the hidden charts. Eventually he abandons the safe world of ledgers to become Ines's apprentice, learning to listen to the water's language.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Young adult, slightly younger than Ines

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Second apprentice; harbour office clerk; later Ines's assistant cartographer

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To understand why the future matters more than the present; to serve a meaningful purpose

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: Uncertainty and change; the inadequacy of numbers to capture truth

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Careful, measured, but growing more confident as he learns

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The Lighthouse Chart

name: Harbour Master Roland Vetch
summary: City official responsible for the harbour archives and official charting work. Courteous but calculating, he seeks to control knowledge of the bay for the city's political and economic benefit. He pressures Ines to surrender Maestro Kell's hidden charts and publishes his own inferior survey in competition.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Sixties

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Harbour Master; keeper of official archives; city administrator

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To maintain institutional control over knowledge and power

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: Loss of authority; private individuals wielding knowledge the city needs

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Formal, diplomatic, carefully kind as a tool of pressure

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The Official Letter

name: Mother Venn
summary: Archivist at the harbour office, a weathered woman who once worked the boats. She understands the patterns of water and recognizes the weight of Maestro Kell's hidden knowledge. She becomes a quiet ally to Ines, understanding that some secrets serve a purpose greater than institutional storage.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Sixty years old

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Harbour archivist; keeper of official records

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To preserve knowledge responsibly; to honor Maestro Kell's memory

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: What happens when knowledge becomes property

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Grounded, practical, with deep wisdom from lived experience

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: A Matter of Archives

name: Garrett Thorne
summary: Merchant captain who discovered Maestro Kell's body and recognizes the danger of the hidden knowledge. He warns Ines about coming threats and stands witness to her decisions. Pragmatic but honorable, he navigates between institutional power and individual integrity.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Middle-aged

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Merchant captain; witness and informal advisor

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To protect those who understand the water; to see justice done

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: Powerful men using knowledge as a weapon

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Direct, measured, carrying the weight of hard choices

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The Apprentice's Dilemma

name: Aurel Danse
summary: Brilliant rival cartographer from Salthaven who studied with Maestro Kell decades earlier. Ambitious and profit-driven, he pursues the bay's charts to sell them to merchants and speculators. He represents the corruption of knowledge into mere information, lacking the patience to truly listen to the water.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Forty years old

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Master cartographer; rival; merchant of information

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To acquire valuable charts and sell them for profit and power

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: Being left behind; losing opportunity to less talented but faster workers

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Smooth, seductive, articulate in presenting reasonable-sounding offers

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The Stranger's Arrival

name: Kess
summary: Elderly tide-reader living by the Narrows, formerly a deep-water captain. He leads a quiet study of water patterns over decades, waiting for understanding to arrive. He recognizes Maestro Kell's charts as confirmation of the tide-readers' own observations and becomes an ally in preserving and publishing the truth.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Elderly

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Tide-reader; observer; keeper of water knowledge

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To understand the water's deep patterns; to ensure knowledge serves listening, not profit

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: That rushed measurement will obscure the water's true voice

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Grave, deliberate, carrying the authority of long observation

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The House by the Narrows

name: Imarys
summary: Middle-aged tide-reader who keeps bird records and astronomical charts. She works alongside Kess and Corvin, contributing her own careful observations to the tide-readers' collective knowledge. She recognizes Maestro Kell's charts as the answer to questions they have been asking for a decade.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Fifties

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Tide-reader; observer of patterns in nature

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To understand how water, birds, stars, and time connect

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: That incomplete understanding will be mistaken for final truth

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Thoughtful, precise, paying attention to connections others miss

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The House by the Narrows

name: Corvin
summary: Younger tide-reader who watches the harbour walls at dawn, marking the water's colour changes. He brings word to Ines from the tide-readers and participates in their systematic survey of the bay. He represents the bridge between the old water-knowledge and the new generation of cartographers.

fields.label: Age
fields.value: Younger adult

fields.label: Role
fields.value: Tide-reader; messenger; collaborator in bay survey

fields.label: Wants
fields.value: To learn the water's language and help others understand it

fields.label: Fears
fields.value: That greed and haste will destroy what takes patience to cultivate

fields.label: Voice
fields.value: Energetic, clear, speaking with quiet urgency about what he has witnessed

fields.label: First appears
fields.value: The House by the Narrows

name: Meddow
summary: A coastal harbour city where the story unfolds. Described as small, with active merchant trade, functioning institutions like a harbour office and city council. The city balances its need for knowledge about the expanding bay with its preference for stability and controlled information flow.

fields.label: Where
fields.value: On the coast, with a harbour, outer islands, and western approaches beyond

fields.label: Look
fields.value: Harbour walls, streets, marketplace, official buildings, dock workers' activity

fields.label: Smell
fields.value: Salt, tar, fish, rope, the everyday work of the water

fields.label: Who is there
fields.value: Merchants, fishermen, dock workers, officials, cartographers, tide-readers

fields.label: Key feature
fields.value: A functioning centre of knowledge-keeping with archives and official authority

name: The Scriptorium
summary: Maestro Kell's workshop where cartographic work is performed. A north-facing room with workbenches, oil lamps, drying charts hanging on walls, carefully maintained instruments and materials. After Maestro Kell's death, it becomes Ines's primary workspace where she continues his tradition of listening to the water through careful measurement and drawing.

fields.label: Where
fields.value: Part of Maestro Kell's household; has access to the harbour

fields.label: Look
fields.value: Workbenches, charts drying on walls, leather cases of tools, stacks of paper, oil lamps

fields.label: Smell
fields.value: Salt stains, old paper, gum arabic, burnt sienna pigment, the patina of careful work

fields.label: Who is there
fields.value: Ines, Thren, occasionally visitors like Garrett Thorne or the tide-readers

fields.label: Significance
fields.value: Sacred space where the water's knowledge is translated into permanent form

name: The Western Approaches
summary: A maze of islands, reefs, and water beyond the Corsair Rocks, four miles from Meddow. Site of the impossible bay that will open through water-driven erosion. Currently dangerous and poorly understood; becomes increasingly navigable and important as the bay develops. The primary focus of all cartographic and tide-reading work in the narrative.

fields.label: Where
fields.value: Four miles beyond the Corsair Rocks; accessible by fishing boat

fields.label: Look
fields.value: Outer islands, shale cliffs, rocks of varying sizes, water channels, eventually a sheltered bay

fields.label: Smell
fields.value: Open water, salt spray, mineral depths, the smell of significant changes in weather

fields.label: Who is there
fields.value: Surveyors, tie-readers, Ines and Thren, Danse's hired men, eventually merchants

fields.label: Significance
fields.value: Where the future is becoming visible; the bay that changes everything

name: The Narrows
summary: A narrow house leaning toward the water, home to the tide-readers Kess, Imarys, and Corvin. Built a hundred years prior by a merchant family, now occupied by people who value knowledge over profit. Its upper room contains working maps, tide tables, instruments, and centuries of accumulated observation about water patterns.

fields.label: Where
fields.value: Near the harbour, by channels called the Narrows, accessible by narrow steep stairs

fields.label: Look
fields.value: Narrow, leaning toward water, worn stone stairs, small windows with water views

fields.label: Smell
fields.value: Salt spray, lamp oil, the particular richness of sustained observation

fields.label: Who is there
fields.value: Kess, Imarys, Corvin, occasionally Ines carrying important knowledge

fields.label: Significance
fields.value: Sacred space where water knowledge is preserved and verified through generations

name: The Copper-Bound Folder
summary: Maestro Kell's hidden collection of charts showing the bay as it will be in the future. Bound in copper with verdigris-darkened edges, it contains six charts dated over fourteen months, increasingly detailed and accompanied by annotations and predictions marked in red ink. It becomes the physical centre of conflict and protection throughout the narrative.

fields.label: What it is
fields.value: Six charts documenting an impossible bay opening in the western approaches; Maestro Kell's life work

fields.label: Where kept
fields.value: Behind bound ledgers on an upper shelf in the scriptorium; later copied and distributed

fields.label: Why it matters
fields.value: Proves Maestro Kell's understanding; shows the water's own deep intentions; worth fortune and danger

fields.label: Key annotations
fields.value: 'WHEN THE WATER REMEMBERS WHAT IT USED TO BE, IT WILL FIGHT TO GO BACK'

fields.label: Fate
fields.value: Copied by Ines into her own hand; shared with tide-readers; knowledge becomes public

name: The Salt Marks
summary: Places where the water leaves permanent records of its movements through salt stains and deposits on rocks. Maestro Kell discovers they can be read like written text to understand not just where water has been but where it intends to go. This understanding becomes key to Ines realizing that the bay is not a prediction but a memory the water is reclaiming.

fields.label: What it is
fields.value: Salt stains, deposits, and marks left by water on rocks and cliffs

fields.label: Where kept
fields.value: On outer rocks and cliffs of the western approaches; visible at low tide

fields.label: Why it matters
fields.value: Reveals water's intention; shows ancient patterns repeating; proves bay has existed before

fields.label: Key insight
fields.value: 'The salt marks do not lie. The water leaves a record of where it has been, and from that record one can read where it wishes to go'

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: The bay is not new; it is the water remembering and reclaiming what it used to be
